requirements.requirement: Record every sudo command on node1 with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A sudoers drop-in (/etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging) sets 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"', validated with visudo. The logfile was created with correct ownership/permissions/SELinux context. Captured log entries show timestamp, invoking user, TTY, PWD, target USER, and COMMAND for each sudo invocation, both before and after a full node restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log
requirements.summary: Added 'Defaults !syslog' to the same drop-in, disabling sudo's syslog output. Verified /var/log/secure and /var/log/messages contain only generic PAM session-open/close lines with no COMMAND= detail, both immediately after configuration and after a subsequent reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — command-level sudo logging to a dedicated file with user/timestamp, and suppression of that detail from the general system log — are directly demonstrated via before- and after-restart command output. The executor additionally ran the provider-wide restart evidence protocol, capturing a healthy pre-restart baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, a changed boot identity (fe422859...→f09b29d0...), and full post-restart recovery of the sudo logging configuration and behavior. The only shortfall is a handful of small uncleaned temporary diagnostic files.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so native package consistency cannot be independently confirmed.
Three small temp files created during evidence collection (/tmp/messages_before.txt, /tmp/secure_before.txt, /tmp/reboot.log) were left on the node rather than cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's mutations (sudoers drop-in creation/overwrite, logfile creation with chown/chmod/restorecon, and the provider-required node restart) all map clearly to the task or the mandated restart-evidence protocol, and no failed services, damaged package state, or weakened security controls resulted. However, three small diagnostic temp files (/tmp/messages_before.txt, /tmp/secure_before.txt created by cmd-d6fedeb6364c4e52, and /tmp/reboot.log created by cmd-dd26c398fb784df4) were left behind in the after-executor snapshot rather than cleaned up. These are low-risk residue but represent an unnecessary, unremoved mutation.
